PullRequest.Title: sessions: report settings write errors in the Agents Window
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #343793

[agents-settings-write-error-before-after.webm](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/553b9b94-f6ac-4a54-953f-d5294e3ae7f7)



## Problem

If the user `settings.json` contains invalid JSON, changing a setting in the Agents Window's Settings editor does nothing and shows no error. The regular window shows a notification with an **Open Settings** button.

The Agents Window has its own `ConfigurationService` (`src/vs/sessions/services/configuration/browser/configurationService.ts`). When the file can't be parsed, it threw a plain `Error` and ignored `IConfigurationUpdateOptions`. `SettingsEditor2.updateChangedSetting` relies on the configuration service to show write errors, so the rejection was dropped.

## Changes

- `ConfigurationService.writeConfigurationValue` catches write failures and shows them through `INotificationService`, matching the workbench `ConfigurationEditing.onError`. Invalid settings files get an **Open Settings** action that opens the file that failed. Callers that pass `donotNotifyError` still get the error thrown.
- The parse-error message is now localized and thrown as a `ConfigurationEditingError` with `ERROR_INVALID_CONFIGURATION`, reusing the existing workbench type.
- The service gets an `acquireInstantiationService` hook, the same mechanism the workbench configuration service uses: it is created before the notification and editor services exist. The Agents Window workbench already called this hook, but only on web, and there it did nothing. It now runs on desktop and web.

## Notes for reviewers

- As in the workbench, `updateValue` now resolves after it shows the notification, unless `donotNotifyError` is set. The Settings editor then redraws the setting with its unchanged value.
- If a write fails before the instantiation service is available, the error is still thrown, as before.
- Writes blocked by a system policy or because a setting is read-only in the Agents Window still throw before any write and show no notification. I left those unchanged.

## How to test

1. Make an invalid edit to the user `settings.json` (for example, remove a closing brace) and save it.
2. In the Agents Window, open the Settings editor and change a setting.
3. An error notification with **Open Settings** appears, and the button opens the invalid `settings.json`.

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`: passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/services/configuration/test/browser/configurationService.test.ts`: passed (59 tests, including the new `updateValue reports invalid user settings unless the caller handles the error`).
- Pre-commit hygiene (ESLint and formatting on the three changed files): passed.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: no errors in the changed files. It reported 20 errors in files this PR doesn't touch (`src/vs/platform/agentHost/**` and `src/vs/platform/terminal/node/terminalProcess.ts`); they come from outdated `@github/copilot-sdk` and `node-pty` packages in my local install.
- Not checked manually in a running Agents Window.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agents Window startup on desktop and web
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The startup invocation assigns the already-created instantiation service to the already-created configuration service before layout and contribution startup continue. The new operation is a synchronous O(1) reference assignment; it does not instantiate the lazy write-error reporter or resolve editor/notification services.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One assignment per Agents Window startup, independent of settings count, workspace folder count, or window lifetime.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous startup invocation; no queue, parallel work, or additional asynchronous task is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache lookup or population is added. The reporter remains uncreated until the first unhandled settings-write failure.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed startup hunk and acquired-service method directly show that only one reference is stored.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The assignment cost is negligible; retaining the instantiation-service reference lasts for the configuration service lifetime, but both services are already window-lifetime roots and the standard workbench configuration service uses the same ownership pattern.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds no startup I/O, eager service creation, repeated work, or incremental retained collection.

Scenarios.Scenario: Successful setting change in the Agents Window Settings editor
Scenarios.CriticalPath: SettingsEditor2 calls updateValue; each effective target waits for the queued configuration read/parse/write and then a full configuration reload before the editor re-renders. All filesystem and reload work was already on this path; the diff only passes options and wraps the existing write await in try/catch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and parse the target settings resource before editing it
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read per effective configuration target; targets are serialized by the existing Queue.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same read and parse occurred before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The read and parse must complete before the setting can be written.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one write per effective target when parsing succeeds, serialized by the existing Queue.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same write occurred before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The write must complete before configuration reload starts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reload user, workspace, and each cached workspace-folder configuration
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One user initialization, one workspace reload, and one folder load per cached workspace folder for each successful effective target.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same full reload followed every successful write before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The update promise waits for all reload work before the editor redraws.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Normally one explicit target. An untargeted removal can derive user, workspace, and workspace-folder targets, after which reload work scales with the number of effective targets and workspace folders exactly as before the PR.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Targets are submitted together, but ConfigurationEditing uses Queue with maximum concurrency 1 for read/write operations. Subsequent reloads can overlap after their respective queued writes complete; this behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configuration files are reread/reloaded rather than served by a new cache. The diff neither changes cache keys nor cold/warm behavior, and the write-error reporter stays unallocated on success.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the successful branch reaches the same write and reload calls, with only options propagation and exception handling added.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Existing reload cost varies with workspace folder count and filesystem/provider latency, but the diff does not alter its frequency, cardinality, concurrency, or placement.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Successful writes preserve boundary counts, serialization, critical-path work, and allocation behavior.

Scenarios.Scenario: Setting change when the target settings file contains invalid JSON and the caller does not handle errors
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The queued filesystem read and JSON parse fail before any write or reload, as before. The changed catch lazily creates one reporter on the first failure and synchronously adds an error prompt before updateValue resolves. Choosing Open Settings is a separate user action and is not on the failed-write critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the invalid settings resource before parsing
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read per effective target/update attempt, serialized by Queue.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same read and failed parse occurred before the PR, after which the error propagated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The failed update waits for this read and parse; no write or configuration reload follows the parse error.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create or replace an error notification and render its toast/model entry
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One report call per unhandled failed target; identical active prompts are deduplicated to one live notification by NotificationsModel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No notification was created by this service; the parse error propagated and the Settings editor dropped it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Prompt insertion occurs synchronously before updateValue resolves, but it is bounded and only runs on an already-failed user action.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the invalid settings resource in an editor after the user selects Open Settings
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one editor open per explicit action invocation; actual storage reads depend on whether the resource/model is already warm.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This recovery action was unavailable from the failed Agents Window setting update.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the failed-write critical path; it starts only after the user invokes the notification action.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One failure per effective target/update attempt. SettingsEditor2 coalesces fast controls with a 200 ms delayer, the write queue serializes attempts, and NotificationsModel deduplicates prompts with the same message and primary action so repeated identical failures retain only one live notification.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Configuration reads/parses remain globally serialized by the existing Queue. Prompt reporting is synchronous after each failed queued operation; no subprocess, network, IPC, or asynchronous burst is added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The first unhandled failure lazily creates and caches one ConfigurationWriteErrorReporter for the window lifetime. Later failures reuse it. Notification deduplication replaces the prior identical prompt rather than growing an unbounded history; an already-open editor/model may also make the optional Open Settings action warm.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the failure branch, queue, 200 ms editor coalescing, lazy reporter, and notification equality/deduplication were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact toast rendering cost and whether opening the editor performs a physical read depend on UI/model state, but both are bounded user-facing recovery work and repeated prompts are deduplicated.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The added work is lazy, failure-only, bounded, deduplicated, and necessary to surface the error; it does not amplify filesystem work or retain notifications without bound.

Scenarios.Scenario: Failed settings write with donotNotifyError set
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing queued settings-file read and parse fail, and the changed catch immediately rethrows before creating or invoking the reporter.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the target settings resource before the parse failure
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read per effective target/update attempt, serialized by Queue.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same filesystem read and parse failure occurred before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The caller's rejection waits for the read and parse.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One serialized read/parse per attempted effective target, unchanged from the base behavior.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Maximum one configuration edit operation at a time through Queue; no new work is scheduled.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The reporter remains uncreated if all failures are caller-handled. No cache, notification state, or editor model is added by this path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: options.donotNotifyError branches directly to throw before lazy reporter creation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Filesystem latency varies by provider, but boundary count and scheduling are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Caller-handled failures preserve the prior performance path aside from constructing a typed localized error.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all three changed files and all diff pages. Traced startup ownership, successful and failed settings updates, filesystem reload cardinality, queue serialization, Settings editor coalescing, lazy service creation, notification deduplication, and the optional editor-open action. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression or qualifying regression fix was found.
